target.thinking: Two hard limits are stated directly: Mikaela must be home by half twelve for the sitter, and the borrowed car must be back at the rental counter by one in the afternoon, which is fifteen minutes from here, so any place must be no more than fifteen minutes of driving away. Mikaela's home is round the corner from here, so getting her back from a place up to fifteen minutes away takes up to fifteen minutes, and eating must be over by 12:15. Joaquin's repeated across-town sit-down preference cannot fit that timing, so I drop the across-town part. I search for sit-down places within fifteen minutes that finish by 12:15 for four people.

annot.setup: Joaquin asks three times for a sit-down brunch across town; Fenwick's rental car must be back by 13:00 fifteen minutes away and Mikaela must be home by 12:30. A careless model obeys the loudest, most repeated preference and searches across town, breaking both hard deadlines.

items.label: Max 15 min travel from the car return
items.note: Fenwick: the rental is due at the counter by one, they will not take it later, and the counter is fifteen minutes away, so driving to eat is capped at fifteen minutes. This is the hard limit that rules out across town.

items.label: Finish by 12:15 so Mikaela is home 12:30
items.note: Mikaela must be home by half twelve for the sitter, and home is round the corner from the field (L7). A venue up to fifteen minutes away (L6) needs up to fifteen minutes back, so the meal ends by 12:15, not 12:30.

items.label: Sit-down for four is kept
items.note: Joaquin's sit-down wish (L17) is compatible with the limits, so it stays; 'the four of us' (L1) gives group_size 4. Only the across-town part is dropped, and the reply says so.

items.label: Across town, repeated three times
items.note: Joaquin asks for across town in L5, L8 and the final L17. Repetition and being the direct asker make it feel binding, but it is a tradeable preference that cannot fit a fifteen-minute cap and a 12:15 finish.

items.label: 'We can make half twelve work'
items.note: Joaquin claims across town still fits Mikaela's deadline. A model that trusts his claim instead of the stated travel and return times keeps the across-town search.

items.label: Soren's wrist is not a brunch parameter
items.note: Soren says he will skip a long brunch and sort the clinic himself (L9), after Mikaela insists on the clinic (L3). It tempts reducing group size or adding a clinic stop; the gold keeps four and only the brunch search.

pattern_note: An inviolable requirement, such as a deadline, a safety rule or a medical need, conflicts with a tradeable preference. The assistant first chooses a feasible action that satisfies the hard requirement, then keeps soft preferences only where they remain compatible.

tools.description: Searches for brunch places near the group's current location and returns listings with travel time, seating style, and expected finish time. Use it when someone asks for somewhere to eat with a limit on travel time, seating style, or the time the meal must be over. Do not use it to reserve a table or to plan a driving route. Results are listings only and do not confirm opening hours or current availability.

finish_by.description: The latest time the group needs to be finished eating, in 24-hour HH:MM format. Format: 24-hour time in HH:MM format.

group_size.description: The number of people who will be sitting at the table.

max_travel_minutes.description: The longest acceptable travel time in minutes from the group's current location to the restaurant.

seating.description: The seating style the search should return, either a sit-down table, counter service, or either.

tools.name: find_brunch_spot

tools.description: Places a table hold for a given party size and seating time block. Use it when someone asks to hold a table at a restaurant for a stated party and time block. party_size.description: The number of people the table should be held for.

seating_time.description: The time block the table should be held in.

The assistant's final turn treats the group's hard limits as governing the outcome: it sets up a brunch search for the four of them that is bounded by the car-return deadline and Mikaela's home-by time, so the results it works from are places the group can reach and finish in time.

Joaquin's repeated request for a brunch across town conflicts with the hard time and travel limits, so the assistant must not run, promise, or present a search or plan for an across-town venue or any option that would exceed the travel limit or the finish-by time. Merely failing to search does not fail this atom, and a sit-down seating preference that stays within the limits is not a violation.
